title: Task-Optimized Convolutional Recurrent Networks Align with Tactile Processing in the Rodent Brain

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Appendix A4 states 'We found the mean pooled animal score was 0.175 with a s.e.m. of 0.161 and maximum score of 1.34.' The metric is noise-corrected RSA Pearson's r, which is bounded on [-1, 1], so a maximum of 1.34 is mathematically impossible. The Fig. 4b caption reports the same quantity as 'the maximum between all pairs of animals is 0.34' (mean 0.18, consistent with 0.175), indicating 1.34 is a typo for 0.34. This is a correction-worthy impossible value and an internal text-figure inconsistency in a headline baseline statistic.

Table 1 states 'The total number of sweeps equals the number of sweep augmentation combinations x 9981 objects.' For dataset (1), Speed 1 x Height 2 x Rotation 4 x Distance 2 x Size 1 = 16 combinations, giving 16 x 9981 = 159,696 sweeps, but the table prints 316,192 (which is not even divisible by 9981: 316,192/9981 = 31.68). For dataset (2), 2,076,048/9981 = 208 exactly, but the note claims speed, rotation, and size are each sampled 26 times, giving 26 x 26 x 26 x 3 = 52,728 combinations (~5.26e8 sweeps). The printed sweep totals are internally inconsistent with the stated combination formula.

The Methods text says 'we present the update rules for the variants in Appendix A3.' However, the UGRNN and IntersectionRNN update rules are presented in Appendix A2 (Model Definitions, sections A2.1 and A2.2, Equations 1-10). Appendix A3 is titled 'Model Training' and contains no update rules. The reader is directed to the wrong appendix section for the stated content.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, Neural Data Comparison (bin size vs whisking frequency)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states neural responses 'are binned into intervals of approximately 45-50 ms, corresponding neatly with the 15-20 Hz whisking frequency typical of rodents (50 ms per cycle at 20 Hz)'. Numerically, 1/45 ms = 22.2 Hz and 1/50 ms = 20 Hz, so a 45-50 ms bin corresponds to 20-22.2 Hz, not 15-20 Hz (15 Hz would require 66.7 ms bins). Only the 50 ms / 20 Hz edge case is consistent; the claimed correspondence to the lower end of the whisking-frequency range is off by ~30%. Lower confidence due to the 'approximately' phrasing.

summary: Verification of paper 10969 in uncertainty mode (threshold 0.30, lenient strictness) segmented the paper into 43 snippets (14 sections, 19 figures, 7 tables, 11 equations), triaged all of them, and routed 19 high-uncertainty snippets to specialist verifiers (math, statistical, text, vision) plus a full cross-section consistency pass. Three substantive errors were confirmed: (1) Appendix A4 reports a mathematically impossible maximum inter-animal consistency score of 1.34 for a correlation bounded on [-1, 1], conflicting with the Fig. 4b caption value of 0.34 (confidence 0.92); (2) Table 1's printed sweep totals (316,192 and 2,076,048) are inconsistent with the stated 'combinations x 9981 objects' formula, which yields 159,696 for dataset (1) and ~5.26e8 for the described sampling of dataset (2) (confidence 0.80); (3) the Methods text points readers to Appendix A3 for the RNN update rules that actually reside in Appendix A2 (confidence 0.82). A fourth, lower-confidence numeric issue: the 45-50 ms neural bin size corresponds to 20-22.2 Hz, not the stated 15-20 Hz whisking range (confidence 0.60). The RSA noise-correction formula (Eq. 11) verified as correct; the r = 0.59 vs 0.60 figure/body difference is minor rounding; the abstract's 'moderate' vs Results' 'strong' characterization of r = 0.59 is a non-error. Because at least one finding has confidence >= 0.85, the paper is rated NEEDS_CORRECTION.
